newsitem.title: USA: Trustmark gets preliminary court approval.
newsitem.headline: Trustmark gets preliminary court approval.

text.p: Trustmark National Bank on Thursday said it received preliminary court approval of a settlement of a class action, in which the firm would pay $4 million in cash and forgive uncollected debt.

The suit involved the purchase of collateral protection insurance, or CPI, for certain Trustmark borrowers. The proposed settlement, filed in United States District Court for the Southern District of Mississippi, is subject to final court approval.
CPI premiums were paid by Trustmark and charged to borrowers who failed to provide proof that they had maintained insurance on their loan collateral.

Notice of the settlement and of a hearing scheduled for April 14, 1997, at the United States Courthouse in Biloxi will be mailed on December 2 to approximately 11,000 Trustmark borrowers, the company said.
Trustmark denies any wrongdoing or liability regarding the use of CPI, Trustmark said.
